identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study of Paclitaxel Combined With Apatinib and Adebrelimab in Gastric/Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Study of Paclitaxel (Albumin-bound) Combined With Apatinib and Adebrelimab in the Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Gastric/Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma Following Previous Immunotherapy Progression

leadSponsor.name: The First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University

descriptionModule.briefSummary: To evaluate the initial efficacy and safety of paclitaxel for injection (albumin-bound) in combination with apatinib mesylate and adebrelimab in the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma following the progression of previous immunotherapy.

armGroups.label: Single arm
armGroups.description: Paclitaxel for injection (albumin-bound) in combination with Apatinib mesylate and adebrelimab

interventions.name: Paclitaxel for injection (albumin-bound)
interventions.description: 100 mg/m2, day 1, day 8, every 21 days for a cycle.

interventions.name: Adebrelimab
interventions.description: 20mg/kg or 1200mg, the first day, every 21 days as a cycle.

interventions.name: Apatinib mesylate
interventions.description: 250mg once a day for 5 consecutive days and discontinue for 2 days

primaryOutcomes.description: Refers to the proportion of all subjects with the best overall response (BOR) as complete remission (CR) or partial remission (PR) according to RECIST 1.1 criteria.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Refers to the proportion of all subjects with the best overall response (BOR) according to RECIST1.1 criteria as complete remission (CR), partial remission (PR) and stable disease (SD).

PFS was defined as the subject's date from the date of the first dose to the date of the first documented tumor progression (as assessed by RECIST1.1 criteria, with or without continuation of treatment) or the date of death from any cause, whichever occurred first.
